original_description: Gather performance evidence without changing the code - profile to find where time or memory goes (Python, Node, Bun, browser, Bash), benchmark and compare two versions/branches/runtimes with interleaved runs and a confidence-interval verdict, verify someone's claimed speedup by independent re-measurement, or review a diff/PR for performance regressions with measured confirmation. Use this skill whenever the user asks to profile, find a bottleneck or hotspot, "why is this slow", "where is the time going", "what's using the memory", wants a flame graph, asks to benchmark or compare implementations, "is this faster", "did this regress", "is this speedup real", "will this PR be slow", "check this for perf issues", or hands you a .prof, .cpuprofile, speedscope, trace.json or benchmark JSON. To change code to make it faster use perf-optimize; to add CI gates use perf-ci.
best_description: Use this skill to get trustworthy performance numbers by actually running and measuring, without editing the code. Covers: finding where CPU time or memory goes (profiling, flame graphs, memory growth or leaks, slow endpoints or scripts; Python, Node, Bun, browser, Bash); benchmarking or comparing two versions, branches, or implementations to decide "is A faster than B?" or "regression or just noise?" with repeated interleaved runs and confidence intervals; checking whether a claimed speedup is real; and reviewing a diff or PR for performance problems (e.g. quadratic loops) and confirming them by running it. Also use when handed profiler or benchmark output (.prof, .cpuprofile, speedscope, trace.json, criterion or benchmark JSON) to interpret. Trigger on the user's wish for evidence ("numbers I can trust", "just tell me what's holding the memory", "confirm by running it"), even if they never say "profile" or "benchmark". Do not use to make code faster (perf-optimize) or add CI perf gates (perf-ci).
final_description: Use this skill whenever a performance question needs an answer backed by real measurement rather than guesswork or code reading. That includes: a slow endpoint, function, script or page where the user wants to know why, where the time or memory is going, or what is leaking (profiling, flame graphs, hotspots); "is A faster than B?" comparisons of branches, versions or implementations, where timeit-style one-off runs aren't enough; "did we regress or is it noise?" questions, including when given benchmark or profiler output (criterion, benchmark.json, .prof, .cpuprofile, speedscope, trace.json) to interpret; checking whether a claimed speedup is real; and reviewing a diff or PR for performance risks such as quadratic loops, then confirming them by running it. Applies to Python, Node, Bun, browser and shell code. It diagnoses and measures only: to actually make code faster use perf-optimize, and for CI perf gates use perf-ci.
